newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower in nervous trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower in nervous trade.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Wednesday but were down far less than on Tuesday as the market fretted over continued political uncertainty and the sharp decline of the shekel, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares ended down 0.53 percent, or 1.53 points, to 288.02 on all-share turnover of 170 million shekels against 188 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.83 percent lower at 295.67.
"The market is extremely nervous. The shekel fell sharply and the political situation is bizarre," said Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities.
The shekel has fallen by almost three percent since Friday after the central bank lowered its key lending rate 1.2 percentage points and the cabinet approved an exchange rate reform.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday delayed a shakeup of his fractious cabinet that is expected to give the former general Ariel Sharon the finance portfolio. On Tuesday night, the government narrowly survived a parliamentary no-confidence vote in which some coalition members abstained.
Ronen Kaufman of Nesuah Trading and Investments said investors were worried about the appointment of Sharon. "Sharon's history is connected with deficits rather than with fiscal discipline," he said.
Kaufman added that the impact of the weaker shekel is not clear. "Basically it's good for exporters but a sharp rise of dollar might lead to rising inflation and to an interest rate hike," he said.

He said the outlook for the market is nevertheless positive. "This is only a healthy technical correction and in the long run the market will continue to rise. The fact that volume was relatively low shows that this is only a consolidation."
"The market made a very big move and prices are not so cheap anymore. The market can not rise forever and I think that this is very healthy," Tsur said.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which gained 1.5 percent at 563 agorot on turnover of 16.8 million shekels; Israel Discount Bank, which fell 0.75 percent to 395 agorot on volume of 10.5 million shekels; and Bank Hapoalim, which lost 0.75 percent to 764 agorot on volume of 5.8 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
